en: The Philippine tarsier has enormous eyes that cannot move in their sockets, so it rotates its head completely around.
The water hyacinth has spongy, air-filled leaf stalks called petioles that allow the plant to float on freshwater.
Carabaos wallow in mud to coat their skin, which protects them from sunburn and helps regulate their body temperature.
Tropical pitcher plants trap and digest insects using modified leaves shaped like deep cups filled with digestive fluids.
Ferns reproduce using microscopic spores located in brown clusters called sori on the underside of their fronds.
The human pupil automatically shrinks in bright light and expands in the dark to control light entering the eye.
Sweat cools your body down through evaporation, preventing your internal temperature from rising too high during hot weather.
Mangrove seeds, called propagules, germinate while still attached to the parent tree before dropping into the coastal mud.
Seagrass beds in coastal ecosystems serve as crucial nursery habitats where young fish hide from larger predators.
Earthworms improve soil health by burrowing through the dirt, which aerates the ground and helps plant roots absorb water.
The coconut crab uses its massive, powerful claws to crack open hard coconut shells to eat the nutritious flesh inside.
Bamboo plants grow rapidly from underground rhizomes, sometimes adding several centimeters to their height in a single day.
